svg.title: Step 10 · The lanes with auth, through Apify
svg.desc: On a lane with auth, get_forecast runs through Apify's Actor, over Apify's REST API, one request, or over its MCP server, call-actor then get-dataset-items, the build, 18 s and $0.01 pinned on both, the token only in a header. Its items become the same forecast. The other three tools are the twin's, with no auth. A failure falls back to the twin's get_forecast, if 12 s of the answer's 50 are left, and the chip says why. Without a token, the lanes are closed.
svg.text: Step 10 · The lanes with auth, through Apify
The forecast through a paid Actor, behind a token; the rest, and any failure, by the twin
REST · with auth: one request
POST run-sync-get-dataset-items, 20 s
build=1.0.9, timeout=18, $0.01 in the address
authorization: Bearer, masked in the chip
a status: one of our errors
MCP · with auth: Apify's MCP server
opened with the lane: 2025, sessions, 5 s
our pin checked; then call-actor, same limits,
then get-dataset-items, 100 items at most
each POST's status kept (issue 65)
actor.py: the items, as get_forecast's
each checked: shape, the place asked, every day
asked, once each and in order
°C to °F here, when asked
hourly: at most 3 days, its hours alone
A failure: the twin answers
one lane.fallback line, its class, never the token
the twin's get_forecast, if 12 s are left
the chip: ↩ Apify didn't accept our token,
so REST · no auth answered
The other three tools: the twin's
geocode_location, get_current_weather, get_air_quality: the Actor has none of them, so the same door with no auth runs them
Why this way: a run costs about half a cent, capped at one, so it's never retried or cached.
An answer on these lanes has 50 s, the Actor's call 20. Without APIFY_TOKEN, the lanes are closed: the
picker says "needs a token", and a form that names one gets our sentence.
In the tests: the Actor's recorded answers; Apify's REST API and MCP server played back; each fallback
A paid door, capped and pinned, with a free one behind it: the forecast always comes.
The chip says which door answered, and why.
